s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive radicular pain and neuropathic symptoms in the lower extremity
salient_findings: Radicular pain radiating from lower back down the left leg
Mild hypesthesia in the left L5–S1 dermatome
Cystic mass in the left L5–S1 foraminal zone extending along the course of the sciatic nerve
key_facts: 8-month history of radicular pain
Pain radiates from lower back down the left leg
Occasional tingling
No weakness or autonomic symptoms
No history of trauma or injury
Mild hypesthesia in the left L5–S1 dermatome
Normal muscle strength
Normal abduction and adduction
Negative Lasègue, Kernig, Bragard, and Sicard signs
Electromyography shows neuropathic irritation of the left L4, L5, S1, and S2 roots
Lumbosacral MRI reveals a solitary, completely cystic mass in the left L5–S1 foraminal zone
Mass measures approximately 13.9 cm in length and 1.9 cm in maximal diameter
Mass is hypointense on T1-weighted images and hyperintense on T2-weighted images
Mass demonstrates peripheral rim enhancement

shortlist.label: Schwannoma
shortlist.why_kept: Matched with the clinical presentation of a solitary, cystic mass along the course of the sciatic nerve, and characteristic MRI findings of hypointensity on T1-weighted images and hyperintensity on T2-weighted images with peripheral rim enhancement

shortlist.label: Neurofibroma
shortlist.why_kept: Considered due to the presence of a cystic mass along the nerve, although less likely than schwannoma given the specific MRI characteristics

shortlist.label: Tarlov cyst
shortlist.why_kept: Possible diagnosis given the cystic nature of the mass and its location in the nerve root region, but less likely than schwannoma

shortlist.label: Ganglion cyst
shortlist.why_kept: Considered as a differential due to the cystic nature of the mass, but less likely given the specific location and MRI characteristics

shortlist.label: Neurilemmoma
shortlist.why_kept: Synonym for schwannoma, retained as it matches the clinical presentation and MRI findings

raw.rationale: The presence of a solitary, completely cystic mass in the left L5–S1 foraminal zone that is hypointense on T1-weighted images and hyperintense on T2-weighted images, with peripheral rim enhancement, is most consistent with a Tarlov cyst, which is a type of nerve root cyst that can cause radicular pain and neuropathic symptoms.

rejected.label: Schwannoma
rejected.why: Schwannomas are typically solid tumors that arise from the nerve sheath, whereas the described mass is completely cystic.

rejected.label: Neurofibroma
rejected.why: Neurofibromas are also solid tumors that arise from the nerve sheath and are often associated with neurofibromatosis type 1, which is not mentioned in the vignette.

rejected.label: Ganglion cyst
rejected.why: Ganglion cysts are typically found in the joints or tendons and are not usually associated with nerve roots or the spinal canal.

rejected.label: Neurilemmoma
rejected.why: Neurilemmoma is another term for schwannoma, which is a solid tumor that does not match the cystic appearance of the described mass.
